threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the tube’ instead of ‘the Overground’—that’s a sure sign you’re new to Dalston.
The 196 night bus pulled up and a guy stepped off with a full suit and a pineapple. No idea where he was headed, but it made the whole stop pause.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I lived here when the kebab shop owner started recommending his favorite wine to me. It's the little things, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can enjoy spontaneous street performances paired with currywurst at midnight, a blend of culture and culinary that's uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to bring a sweater, even in summer—Fog City is real, and the weather is a constant surprise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy lecturing tourists on Muni etiquette while waiting for the 21. Call me crazy, but it felt like prime Tenderloin performance art.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always stop for ice cream at Joan Blanques, not realizing the best scoop is at the tiny gelateria on Carrer de l’Escorial. It's a local secret.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers—they're the ones still looking at maps trying to figure out which way is east when the sun’s setting.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think of the Dalston Junction as a station, not just a spot to grab a coffee and watch the world go by.
Last week on the 333, a bloke was serenading the bus with an old Hendrix tune, while a lady quietly knitted. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I had to dodge a man selling fresh gebrannte Mandeln on the corner while a busker played Offspring. Classic Neukölln chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you get techno parties in abandoned buildings where the bouncers know your regular drink order by heart, no matter how long it's been.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're local when they casually mention a BART delay like it’s the weather forecast, not a life crisis.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy hop off the 5, toss a burrito at a street performer, and keep walking. Classic San Francisco chaos!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but it’s the local bars and hidden plazas where the real soul of the neighborhood lies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered look while trying to figure out the TMB app—real locals always just check the nearest 'parada' sign.
